title: Dead & Company website
lede: The band’s site after its 2026 Golden Gate Park shows: fat, outlined concert-poster lettering and a stippled drawing on full-bleed yellow.
summary: Full-bleed yellow, pink and light-blue outlined display lettering, and a stippled Golden Gate Bridge.

evidence.note: Captured with `tools/capture.mjs` (headless Chrome, 1440 × 900) on 28 September 2026 and inspected. The screenshot shows the first viewport; the measurement covers up to four screens.

styles.note: Borderline: a full-bleed saturated ground, centered layout, and fat display lettering with echo outlines, but the letters stay legible and the body type is a clean geometric sans. The colors do not vibrate.

observed: A saturated golden yellow fills the whole viewport.
DEAD & COMPANY is centered at the top in very fat, tight capitals filled with pink, with a black outline and a black offset shadow.
GOLDEN GATE PARK sits below in tall condensed capitals filled with light blue and outlined in black, with an offset black shadow.
Smaller lines, CELEBRATING 60 YEARS OF THE GRATEFUL DEAD’S MUSIC and SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA, are in a wide black geometric sans.
A stippled drawing of the Golden Gate Bridge in light blue, green, and black, with a DEADCO blimp, fills the lower half.
The navigation at top right is plain black text and social icons.
interpretation: The page borrows the poster tradition of its own subject, the Grateful Dead, through lettering and a colored ground. It stops short of the style’s distortion and ornament.
Measured values: `color.chromaticShare` 0.73 and `type.centerShare` 1.0 pass; `color.hues` is 2, `surface.radius.median` is 0, and `color.patternShare` is 0, because the stipple is an image.
borrow: Give display lettering a fill color, a black outline, and an offset black shadow for a poster look that stays legible.
Use a saturated yellow as the page ground instead of white.

images.alt: Dead and Company home page: yellow background, pink outlined DEAD & COMPANY lettering, light-blue outlined GOLDEN GATE PARK lettering, a thank-you line in black, and a stippled drawing of the Golden Gate Bridge with a blimp.
